summary.title: CodeRabbit | Governance & Control for Agentic Development
summary.one_liner: CodeRabbit is a commercial AI code review product covering automated PR reviews, PR triage, change explanations, and continuous security monitoring.
keywords: reduce false positives in security scans
takeaways: CodeRabbit positions itself as a validation layer for code written by coding agents, with AI reviews on GitHub and GitLab.
Triage features score, rank, and route PRs, including auto-assigning reviewers and a Kanban board for the PR queue.
Change Stack offers semantic diffs, blast radius context, and architectural diagrams to help understand large diffs.
CodeRabbit Security offers scheduled deep scans and scans on every PR, and says it verifies findings before fixing them in a PR.
The page is mainly marketing; it gives no pricing, technical implementation details, or independent benchmarks.
summary.summary: This is the marketing landing page for CodeRabbit, a product for governing AI-generated code changes. It describes four areas: AI code review with customizable Quiet, Chill, and Assertive profiles; Triage, which scores, ranks, and routes pull requests; Change Stack, which aims to help reviewers understand large diffs via semantic diffs, blast radius context, and diagrams; and CodeRabbit Security, which claims continuous monitoring with scheduled and per-PR scans. The page makes claims about customer numbers and context depth but provides few verifiable technical details, and no pricing or setup steps are given.
